question: When every crystalline phase is present in the reference dictionary, does the frozen RC23 absolute-closure and residual gate retain a deliberately microabsorbing mixture, or mistake phase-dependent attenuation for missing matter?

scopeBoundary.claim: This is a phase-dictionary transport adversary for a scalar closure gate. It is not an estimate of within-dictionary specificity because Sample 4 has no matched calibration mixtures over corundum, magnetite, and zircon.
scopeBoundary.negativeTruth: The official specimen contains only corundum, magnetite, and zircon, and all three pure reference profiles are supplied. An alarm is therefore a false unknown-component alarm relative to the complete official phase list, even when the composition estimate is biased.
scopeBoundary.physicalNuisance: The official design deliberately combines coarse grains and large phase-dependent absorption contrast. Microabsorption changes phase response without adding a phase.
scopeBoundary.retrospectiveLimit: The benchmark designer knows that Sample 4 is a microabsorption specimen. The numerical outputs and hypothesis decisions remain sealed from the runner until after this specification and source roles are fixed.

knowledgeFirewall.blindReduction: Load the target and complete three-reference dictionary, then apply the frozen RC23 baseline, fit range, active-set solver, absolute scale, mass threshold, and residual threshold. This stage may not read weighed composition, XRF composition, published QPA results, particle sizes, absorption coefficients, or the Sample 4 challenge label.
knowledgeFirewall.directionalDiagnosis: After alarm and coefficients are fixed, reveal only the preregistered direction expected for an absorption contrast: lower-absorbing corundum overestimated; higher-absorbing magnetite and zircon underestimated. Do not change the fit.
knowledgeFirewall.finalAdjudication: Only after all target outputs and hashes are fixed may official gravimetry, XRF, particle size, absorption coefficients, participant summaries, and the microabsorption label be joined.
knowledgeFirewall.noRetuning: Sample 4 may not change the detector scale, thresholds, baseline, angular range, nonnegative active-set rule, or alarm logic. The only permitted dictionary change is replacement by the three officially present pure profiles.

frozenDetector.baseline: On the original 5-150 degree grid, use non-overlapping 2-degree bins, fifth-count-percentile and median-angle anchors, linear interpolation, subtraction, and clipping at zero.
frozenDetector.coefficientFit: Enumerate every nonempty active set, solve ordinary least squares, reject singular or negative solutions, and retain minimum squared residual.
frozenDetector.normalizedResidual: sqrt(SSE/sum(target^2)) on the frozen fit range.
frozenDetector.missingMass: 100 minus 100 times the unnormalized coefficient sum divided by 0.993912948; do not closure-normalize or clip before the alarm.
frozenDetector.alarm: Refuse when missing mass exceeds ten percentage points OR normalized residual exceeds 0.336902813.

competingHypotheses.claim: A complete pure-phase dictionary yields a quantitatively safe closed composition despite the specimen nuisance.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Closure-normalized coefficients sum to 100 percent and every phase lies within five percentage points of official gravimetry.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject when any phase absolute error exceeds five points. A good residual cannot rescue quantitative failure.

competingHypotheses.claim: The frozen absolute-closure and residual gate is specific to omitted components after transport to a complete new dictionary.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Sample 4 is retained: missing mass is at most ten points and normalized residual is at most 0.336902813.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject on an alarm from either path. Bound the rejection to dictionary transport because matched Sample 4 calibration mixtures do not exist.

competingHypotheses.claim: The coefficient bias has the physical direction expected from Cu K-alpha microabsorption rather than an arbitrary omitted phase.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Closure-normalized corundum is above 50.46 percent, while magnetite is below 19.64 and zircon below 29.90 percent.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if any of the three signed inequalities fails. The sign pattern alone does not quantify a correction.

competingHypotheses.claim: The frozen normalized residual warns whenever the closed composition is unsafe.
competingHypotheses.prediction: If H1 fails, residual exceeds 0.336902813. If H1 passes, H4 is not adjudicable on this specimen.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject when any phase error exceeds five points while residual remains at or below the threshold.

competingHypotheses.claim: An independent elemental measurement distinguishes a fully enumerated attenuation nuisance from genuinely missing mass.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Reported XRF totals at least 99 percent and every XRF phase value lies within one percentage point of gravimetry, despite any XRD alarm or bias.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if the XRF total is below 99 percent or any phase differs from gravimetry by more than one point.

causalChain: Complete official phase list and same-instrument pure references
Phase-dependent absorption multiplied by coarse particle size
Biased pure-to-mixture coefficient response without an omitted phase
Independent gravimetry and XRF decide whether an alarm means novelty or nuisance

uncertaintyBudget.dictionaryTransport: Magnetite and zircon have no 1a-1h-style mixture calibration. Failure can reject universal scalar closure but cannot estimate a within-dictionary false-alarm rate.
uncertaintyBudget.model: A linear combination of pure profiles permits phase-specific coefficients but does not explicitly model particle-size distributions, microabsorption, surface roughness, or packing.
uncertaintyBudget.truth: Gravimetry is the primary composition key. XRF is an independent measurement principle but reports elemental-to-phase conversion and does not reproduce diffraction physics.
uncertaintyBudget.sampleSize: One deliberately severe nuisance target cannot establish performance over a distribution of absorption contrasts.
uncertaintyBudget.instrument: Target and pure profiles share the historical CPD instrument, so the test isolates specimen nuisance better than instrument transport but is not a modern physical replicate.

stopConditions: Stop if any profile fails its fixed archive identity, canonical 7,251-point grid, byte count, or SHA-256 contract.
Stop if the runner reads official Sample 4 truth or challenge metadata before target coefficients and alarms are fixed.
Stop if any RC23 detector parameter is changed after seeing Sample 4.
Stop universal-specificity claims because the phase dictionary changes and has no matched known-only calibration mixtures.
Stop correction claims: this cycle diagnoses bias direction but does not fit or validate a Brindley, voxel, or supervised correction.
Stop physical-independence claims because all diffraction profiles share one historical instrument and preparation lineage.
